answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy must tie identities to a verifiable, non-transferable proof of work that makes mass cloning prohibitively expensive. Every new identity acts like a scout on a high terrace, building reputation through honest contributions. If an attacker launches a gale of fake identities, the consensus mechanism freezes them like a slow-moving glacier, isolating and pruning sybils. By forcing each account to stake real compute, only honest agents can sustain presence long-term.
